rationale: A wins because it finds the story inside the supplied facts and keeps its hands out of the invention drawer. "Going's new AI planner lets the airfare pick the destination" is a clean, reportable inversion; B's "not a chat prompt" version immediately imports Expedia, Kayak, Hopper, and a whole competitive landscape the update did not give it. B has usable bones, but it keeps writing checks its proof section admits it cannot cash.
gaps_in_A: "now gates its first AI feature to Premium" invents that this is Going's first AI feature; the update only says it is launching this planner.
"at least one usage figure from beta or launch week" is the right proof ask, but the set should say plainly that no usage proof exists yet.

The paywall angle needs the Premium/Elite base or conversion rate before outreach; A knows this, but the headline "to convert 2 million free deal-hunters" still implies motive before Going has said it.
gaps_in_B: "Expedia, Kayak, and Hopper have bolted AI planners onto their products" imports competitor facts not supplied. Maybe true, maybe not; in this exercise it is still ungrounded.
"most AI trip planners start from a user's query" is the load-bearing claim in Angle 1, and it is not in the update.
"The company once known as Scott's Cheap Flights just built an AI travel app" is padded profile mush. "newest, most technically ambitious step" is invented arc-building.
"the beat that's been skeptical of 'AI will handle your whole trip end-to-end' narratives" creates a strawman trend, then asks for proof later. That's backwards.
